Hi Laura —

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Attaching our redline of the MSA focused on the Limitation of Liability and the damages carve-outs (see nimbus_msa_redline_v2.pdf). Our commercial team is firm on preserving the one-way exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages in favor of the customer — they view it as standard for our sector.

Key asks in the attached redline:
- One-way exclusion that prohibits Redwood from recovering consequential, special or punitive damages (customer-favored wording).
- Narrow exception language only for IP infringement indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- No duty-to-mitigate carveout language — they think it creates enforcement risk for Nimbus.

We are open to a higher cap where appropriate but won’t accept mutual broadening of exclusions. Please confirm next steps and who on your side will own legal negotiation.

Laura / Karthik —

High-level legal take: accepting a one-way exclusion substantially increases Redwood's exposure and is uncommon for platform vendors. Two immediate concerns:

1) Asymmetric liability combined with a low Order Form cap leaves us exposed to outsized recovery risk for any downstream loss claims; the commercial cap must scale if we consider a one-way exclusion.

2) Removing duty-to-mitigate is risky — it eliminates a basic contractual force that obliges the claimant to take reasonable steps to limit loss. We should retain a duty-to-mitigate phrasing, but we can make it narrowly tailored to avoid operational burden.

Suggested compromise (two options to present):

Option A — Preferred (mutual exclusion, narrow exceptions):
"Each party's liability for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages is excluded to the extent permitted by law, provided that such exclusion shall not apply to (a) a party's indemnification obligations arising from third-party claims for intellectual property infringement, (b) damages resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (c) either party's obligations arising under Sections [Confidentiality / Data Protection / IP]."

Also add: "Each claimant must take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate any loss, including providing prompt notice and cooperating in loss-limitation efforts."

Option B — Commercial concession for One-Way (if customer insists):
- Accept one-way exclusion in favor of customer only if: (i) Order Form cap is increased to [X] (suggested = 3x standard cap or an absolute floor of $5M for enterprise deals), and (ii) we retain the mitigation duty and the IP/gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carveouts.
- Add a reciprocal audit / insurance requirement: customer to maintain cyber liability insurance with minimum limits.

I attached a plain-text snippet with the redlined clause (redline_suggested_clause.txt) that you can drop into a reply.

If you want, I can draft the email to Nimbus with both options and a firm ask for their decision on cap.

-Markus

Thanks Markus — makes sense. A couple of commercial notes from my side:

- For enterprise deals like Nimbus we can reasonably increase the Order Form cap, but we need a clear pricing offset (we should propose either a one-time onboarding fee or a modest increase to the committed monthly spend).
- As a negotiation tactic, we can present Option A (mutual exclusion) as our baseline and indicate willingness to consider Option B only if they accept a higher committed spend or a 12-month minimum term.
- If they insist on one-way + no mitigation, we should escalate to sales leadership. It materially changes our risk profile.

Laura — happy to join a call with their GC if needed.

—Karthik

Ellen —

Appreciate the redline and the clarity on your position. We've reviewed with legal and sales and want to propose a compromise to keep momentum. Please see summary below and the attached proposed redline (proposed_msa_redline_laura_v3.pdf).

Summary of Redwood position / proposed compromise:
- Preferred: Mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, with narrow exceptions for IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and obligations under confidentiality/data protection. We also propose retaining a "commercially reasonable steps to mitigate" clause. (See attached language.)
- If Nimbus will not accept mutual exclusion, we can consider your one-way exclusion request only if Nimbus agrees to BOTH: (1) increase the Order Form cap to a higher floor (suggest starting point: $3M or 3x the standard cap for this engagement), and (2) accept the mitigation duty language and the IP/gross negligence carveouts.
- Additionally, we request confirmation that Nimbus maintains cyber and general liability insurance with commercially reasonable limits, and that both parties will cooperate on incident response.

Please review the attached redline. If you are open to Option A (mutual exclusion) that will expedite execution. If you plan to insist on one-way, indicate whether the increased cap is acceptable so we can route for final internal approvals.

Happy to set a short call with Markus and Karthik if you'd prefer to walk through the tradeoffs live.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
